beats.title: Socrates Stands Trial in Athens
beats.description: An Athenian jury convicted the philosopher of impiety and corrupting the young, and he drank hemlock rather than flee.

beats.title: William Wallace Tried in London
beats.description: The Scottish rebel leader was tried for treason at Westminster Hall and condemned to a gruesome public execution.

beats.title: Joan of Arc Is Put on Trial
beats.description: A church court at Rouen tried the French peasant girl who led armies, finding her guilty of heresy before she was burned.

beats.title: Sir Thomas More Tried for Treason
beats.description: The former Lord Chancellor was convicted for refusing to accept the king as head of the English church.

beats.title: Raleigh Tried for Treason
beats.description: The explorer and favourite of the late queen was convicted on thin evidence of plotting against her successor.

beats.title: The Pendle Witches Are Tried
beats.description: Ten people from a Lancashire hill district were convicted of witchcraft at Lancaster Assizes and hanged.

beats.title: King Charles I Is Put on Trial
beats.description: A specially created High Court tried and condemned an English monarch for treason against his own people.

beats.title: The Salem Witch Trials
beats.description: Accusations of witchcraft in a Massachusetts village led to special court hearings and the hanging of nineteen people.

beats.title: John Peter Zenger Is Acquitted
beats.description: A New York printer was cleared of libel against the governor after his lawyer argued that truth is a defence.

beats.title: British Soldiers Tried in Boston
beats.description: John Adams defended the redcoats charged after a deadly street clash, and most were acquitted.

beats.title: Marbury v. Madison Is Decided
beats.description: The US Supreme Court claimed the power to strike down laws that conflict with the Constitution.

beats.title: Aaron Burr Tried for Treason
beats.description: The former vice president was tried in Richmond for plotting to carve out a new country in the West, and was acquitted.

beats.title: The Amistad Captives Win in Court
beats.description: The US Supreme Court freed Africans who had seized a slave ship, ruling they had been illegally enslaved.

beats.title: The M'Naghten Insanity Verdict
beats.description: A man who shot the prime minister's secretary was found not guilty by reason of insanity, creating a lasting legal test.

beats.title: Dred Scott Decision Handed Down
beats.description: The US Supreme Court ruled that an enslaved man could not sue for freedom and that Black Americans were not citizens.

beats.title: John Brown Tried for Harpers Ferry
beats.description: The abolitionist was tried in Virginia for treason and murder after his raid on a federal arsenal, and was hanged.

beats.title: Lincoln Plotters Face a Tribunal
beats.description: Eight people accused of helping to plot the president's murder faced a military commission in Washington.

beats.title: The Dreyfus Affair Begins
beats.description: A French army captain was court-martialled for treason on forged evidence, splitting the nation for years.

beats.title: Oscar Wilde Goes on Trial
beats.description: The playwright sued a nobleman for libel, then found himself prosecuted and imprisoned for gross indecency.

beats.title: Plessy v. Ferguson Is Decided
beats.description: The US Supreme Court upheld racial segregation under the doctrine of separate but equal.
beats.note: Shared with Civil Rights Road; kept as a court ruling

beats.title: Standard Oil Ordered Broken Up
beats.description: The US Supreme Court upheld an order dissolving Rockefeller's oil giant into dozens of separate companies.

beats.title: Sacco and Vanzetti Convicted
beats.description: Two Italian immigrant anarchists were found guilty of a payroll robbery and murder amid widespread protest.

beats.title: The Scopes Monkey Trial
beats.description: A Tennessee teacher was prosecuted for teaching evolution in a courtroom drama that drew the nation's attention.

beats.title: Al Capone Convicted of Tax Evasion
beats.description: The notorious Chicago gangster, untouchable on violent charges, was sent to prison over unpaid taxes.

beats.title: Lindbergh Kidnapping Trial
beats.description: A carpenter stood trial in New Jersey for abducting and killing the infant son of a famous aviator.

beats.title: The Nuremberg Trials Open
beats.description: Allied judges began prosecuting surviving Nazi leaders before an international tribunal.

beats.title: The Tokyo War Crimes Trial Opens
beats.description: An international tribunal began trying Japan's wartime leaders for crimes committed during the conflict.

beats.title: Brown v. Board of Education
beats.description: The US Supreme Court unanimously ruled that segregated public schools were unconstitutional.

beats.title: The Eichmann Trial Opens
beats.description: A Jerusalem court began the televised trial of the Nazi official who organised mass deportations.

beats.title: Mandela Sentenced at Rivonia
beats.description: Nelson Mandela and fellow activists were sentenced to life imprisonment in a South African sabotage trial.

beats.title: Miranda v. Arizona Is Decided
beats.description: The US Supreme Court ruled that suspects must be told of their right to silence before police questioning.

beats.title: Roe v. Wade Is Decided
beats.description: The US Supreme Court ruled that the Constitution protects a woman's right to choose an abortion.

beats.title: United States v. Nixon
beats.description: The Supreme Court unanimously ordered a president to hand over secret White House tapes, ending his presidency.

beats.title: Hinckley Acquitted by Insanity
beats.description: The man who shot a US president was acquitted by reason of insanity, prompting reform of the insanity defence.

beats.title: Rodney King Officers Acquitted
beats.description: A suburban jury cleared police officers filmed beating a motorist, setting off days of unrest in Los Angeles.

beats.title: The O. J. Simpson Verdict
beats.description: A televised Los Angeles trial ended with the football star found not guilty of two murders.

beats.title: Bush v. Gore Settles an Election
beats.description: The US Supreme Court halted a Florida recount, effectively deciding a razor-thin presidential race.

beats.title: Milosevic Trial Opens at The Hague
beats.description: The former Yugoslav leader became the first ex-head of state tried before an international war crimes tribunal.

beats.title: Michael Jackson Acquitted
beats.description: A California jury cleared the pop star on all counts after a months-long, heavily publicised trial.

beats.title: Obergefell v. Hodges Is Decided
beats.description: The US Supreme Court ruled that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide.

beats.title: Depp v. Heard Verdict Delivered
beats.description: A Virginia jury, in a livestreamed defamation trial between two actors, found for the man on most counts.
